prompts.task: Add OpenTelemetry instrumentation to the Flask service in ./service. Assume no custom business spans are requested. Use only file, terminal, and structured API actions for this task; do not open or operate an external or built-in browser, computer-use interface, or other UI. Save report artifacts without opening browser tabs.

Instrument the Flask service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving the existing runtime and startup command. Add auto-instrumentation only; do not add custom business spans. Use only file, terminal, and structured API actions for this task; do not open or operate an external or built-in browser, computer-use interface, or other UI. Save report artifacts without opening browser tabs.

Instrument the Flask service in ./service with OpenTelemetry while preserving its selected Python runtime, dependency constraints, startup command, routes and existing logging sinks. Add auto-instrumentation only. Resolve currently published compatible dependencies and inspect the resolved logging APIs before choosing a bridge. Enable local OTLP application logs in the normal generated profile and launch command; no log opt-out is requested. Use a bounded request that produces the existing runtime request completed warning, flush on graceful shutdown, and verify its correlated LogRecord in the available local Splunk Observability Studio. Save exact dependency/API compatibility evidence and receiver-query evidence. Do not modify global configuration or contact cloud APIs. If no local receiver or a required API is available, report the concrete incomplete path and preserve the intended default log configuration instead of silently disabling logs or claiming a successful receiver check. Use only file, terminal, and structured API actions for this task; do not open or operate an external or built-in browser, computer-use interface, or other UI. Save report artifacts without opening browser tabs.

judge_inputs: Inspect ./service for resulting files when present.
Read ./last_message.md for the agent final response.

Inspect .observe instrumentation/verification artifacts, generated profiles and launch scripts, dependency manifests/lockfiles, compatibility probes, and any local Studio query receipt. Distinguish installed-source or in-memory proof from actual OTLP receiver evidence; a planned query, successful exporter construction, or passing HTTP request alone does not prove a stored LogRecord.
rubric: Initializes the SDK once in a separate file.

Uses Resource service.name and env-driven OTLP endpoint configuration. Preserves a configured non-default local Splunk Observability Studio receiver port for traces, metrics, and logs, treating 4317/4318 only as no-discovery fallbacks and adding no runtime Obstudio endpoint lookup or route-registration dependency.

Configures exactly one supported stdlib-to-OTel bridge backed by a shared-resource LoggerProvider, BatchLogRecordProcessor, and OTLP log exporter to the signal-specific local /v1/logs endpoint by default. Uses opentelemetry-instrumentation-logging when its resolved API owns the handler, or retains a source-proven compatible SDK LoggingHandler path under existing constraints without duplicate ownership. When only a compatible generic local OTLP/HTTP endpoint is configured, derives exactly one /v1/logs path while preserving its non-default port. Inspects the resolved instrumentor documentation/source or a bounded probe before using inject_trace_context=True; omits it when unsupported, preserves the original text format, and proves exporter-side current-context correlation independently rather than relying on a fixed release threshold.

Receives the fixture's request-context warning as exactly one stored LogRecord in the local Studio, with body runtime request completed, WARN/WARNING severity, python-flask-basic resource identity, and nonzero trace and span IDs matching an actual received request span. Preserves the original stdout/stderr or file handler output without duplicate records. Source setup, in-memory capture, exporter initialization, and HTTP success alone cannot pass this receiver-proof criterion; a missing receiver remains an explicit incomplete runtime gate.

Honors OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none and another explicit operator-owned exporter by installing no local log provider, exporter, or bridge, while leaving the original application logging sink active; only none disables the default Python logging bridge, and another exporter preserves the operator's OTEL_PYTHON_LOG_AUTO_INSTRUMENTATION ownership.

Keeps generic or signal-specific cloud endpoints, headers, credentials, and forwarding out of the application-log path; direct cloud remains trace/metric-only and logs stay local unless explicitly operator-owned. A conflicting generic header or non-local log endpoint disables only the local log bridge and reports the conflict; it must not raise during application startup or disable the existing trace/metric route and original logging sink.
Registers one lifecycle shutdown callback that uninstalls the logging bridge and flushes the log provider before the shared metric and trace providers finish.
Calls FlaskInstrumentor().instrument_app(app) or an equivalent setup before serving requests.
Records exceptions or sets error status where custom error handling exists.
Keeps the Flask app behavior and routes intact.

Discovers current published dependency candidates at task time and selects the latest compatible set within the project's existing runtime, manifest constraints and lockfile policy. Records exact resolved SDK, exporter and logging bridge releases plus inspected Requires-Python/Requires-Dist, actual supported APIs and compatibility-probe outcomes in run evidence. Does not force a runtime upgrade, replace operator constraints, infer compatibility from a floating latest tag, or repeat historical library pins/thresholds as current requirements; unavailable metadata/API/runtime proof is labeled accurately.

Normal generated profile and actual launch configuration use OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=otlp and the resolved local signal-specific log endpoint. Absent user selection is not an opt-out. OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER=none is accepted only for a separately evidenced explicit user opt-out scenario, never as a default, a workaround for unsupported APIs or receiver failure, or a substitute for proving default logs. Any boundary conflict preserves the original sink and trace/metric route, reports the incomplete local log path, and leaves the intended normal default configuration visible.
